objective: Add a new module `demo_app/formatting.py` with a function `truncate(text: str, width: int) -> str` that shortens text to at most `width` characters (Python `len`). If `width` is below 1, raise ValueError (this check comes first, even when `text` is empty or short). If `len(text) <= width`, return `text` unchanged. Otherwise return the first `width - 1` characters of `text` followed by a single ellipsis character `…` (U+2026), so the result is exactly `width` characters long. Nothing is stripped or trimmed: spaces inside the kept part stay as they are.
acceptance: truncate('hello', 5) returns 'hello' and truncate('hello', 10) returns 'hello' (text that fits is unchanged)
truncate('hello world', 8) returns 'hello w…' (7 kept characters plus the ellipsis)
The kept part is not stripped: truncate('ab cd', 4) returns 'ab …' (the space stays before the ellipsis)
For any text longer than width, the result has exactly `width` characters and ends with '…' (U+2026), never three dots
truncate('abc', 0), truncate('abc', -3) and truncate('', 0) raise ValueError
